bcSpouseMax.label: British Columbia spouse and eligible dependant amount, most

bcMedicalThresholdMax.label: British Columbia medical expense threshold, most
bcMedicalThresholdMax.source: BC428 line 50: whichever is less, $2,689 or 3% of net income

bcDonationLowRate.label: British Columbia donation credit rate on the first $200

bcDonationHighRate.label: British Columbia donation credit rate above $200

bcDonationTopRate.label: British Columbia donation credit rate on income in the top bracket
bcDonationTopRate.source: Worksheet BC428, line 58969: 20.5% on the part of donations up to taxable income over $259,829

bcDonationTopThreshold.label: Taxable income where the top British Columbia donation rate starts

bcDividendEligibleRate.label: British Columbia dividend tax credit rate, eligible dividends
bcDividendEligibleRate.source: Worksheet BC428, line 61520: 12% of the taxable amount

bcDividendOtherRate.label: British Columbia dividend tax credit rate, other dividends
bcDividendOtherRate.source: Worksheet BC428, line 61520: 1.96% of the taxable amount

bcTaxReductionLimit.label: Net income from which there is no British Columbia tax reduction
bcTaxReductionLimit.source: BC428: no reduction when net income is $40,807 or more

bcPensionAmountMax.label: Most British Columbia pension income amount

taxBrackets.label: Federal tax brackets
taxBrackets.source: T1 Step 5 Part A. The lowest rate went from 15% to 14% on July 1, 2025, so 14.5% applies for the year. Bases as printed on the form.

creditRate.label: Federal credit rate
creditRate.source: T1 line 114: federal non-refundable tax credit rate for 2025

basicPersonalAmountMax.label: Basic personal amount, full
basicPersonalAmountMax.source: T1 line 30000 and Federal Worksheet: $16,129 when net income is $177,882 or less

basicPersonalAmountMin.label: Basic personal amount, minimum
basicPersonalAmountMin.source: T1 line 30000 and Federal Worksheet: $14,538 when net income is $253,414 or more

basicPersonalAmountPhaseStart.label: Net income where the basic personal amount starts to go down

basicPersonalAmountPhaseEnd.label: Net income where the basic personal amount reaches its minimum
basicPersonalAmountPhaseEnd.source: Federal Worksheet, line 30000: threshold plus the 75,532 range

ageAmountMax.label: Age amount, full
ageAmountMax.source: T1 line 30100 and Federal Worksheet: maximum $9,028 for people born in 1960 or earlier

ageAmountThreshold.label: Net income where the age amount starts to go down

canadaEmploymentAmount.label: Canada employment amount
canadaEmploymentAmount.source: T1 line 31260: whichever is less, $1,471 or employment income

cppBaseRate.label: CPP base rate
cppBaseRate.source: Schedule 8: the base part of the 5.95% employee rate (4.95%) is a credit on line 30800

cppEmployeeMax.label: Most CPP contributions for an employee
cppEmployeeMax.source: CRA payroll table, 2025: maximum employee contribution $4,034.10

cpp2EmployeeMax.label: Most second CPP contributions for an employee
cpp2EmployeeMax.source: CRA payroll table, 2025: CPP2 maximum employee contribution $396

enhancedCppDeductionMax.label: Most deduction for enhanced CPP contributions

medicalThresholdMax.label: Medical expense threshold, most
medicalThresholdMax.source: T1 line 109: whichever is less, $2,834 or 3% of net income

donationLowRate.label: Donation credit rate on the first $200

donationTopRate.label: Donation credit rate on income in the top bracket
donationTopRate.source: Schedule 9 line 20: 33% on the part of donations up to taxable income over $253,414

donationTopThreshold.label: Taxable income where the top donation rate starts

donationIncomeLimit.label: Donation limit, share of net income

topUpThreshold.label: Credits that the 14.5% rate fully covers

tuitionIncomeThreshold.label: Taxable income up to which tuition is limited by taxable income

lowestBracketTop.label: Top of the lowest federal tax bracket
lowestBracketTop.source: T1 Step 5 Part A: taxable income up to $57,375 is taxed at the lowest rate (the first row of taxBrackets)

rrspOverContributionAllowance.label: RRSP contributions allowed above the deduction limit without tax
rrspOverContributionAllowance.source: Form T1-OVP: the 1% monthly tax applies to excess contributions over $2,000

tuitionTransferMax.label: Most current-year tuition a student can transfer

pensionIncomeAmountMax.label: Most pension income amount
pensionIncomeAmountMax.source: Federal Worksheet, line 31400: whichever is less, line 8 or $2,000

oasRecoveryThreshold.label: Net income where OAS starts to be repaid
oasRecoveryThreshold.source: Federal Worksheet, line 23500, line 16: OAS benefits base amount $93,454

eiRepaymentThreshold.label: Net income where EI benefits may be repaid
eiRepaymentThreshold.source: Federal Worksheet, line 23500: line 23400 more than $82,125 with EI on line 11900

cppMaxPensionableEarnings.label: Maximum pensionable earnings (YMPE)
cppMaxPensionableEarnings.source: Schedule 8, Part 2, line B: $71,300 for 12 months

cppAdditionalMaxPensionableEarnings.label: Additional maximum pensionable earnings (YAMPE)
cppAdditionalMaxPensionableEarnings.source: Schedule 8, Part 2, line D: $81,200 for 12 months

cppBasicExemption.label: CPP basic exemption
cppBasicExemption.source: Schedule 8, Part 2, line E: $3,500 for 12 months

cppMaxContributoryEarnings.label: Most earnings subject to base and first additional contributions
cppMaxContributoryEarnings.source: Schedule 8, Part 5, line 19: line B minus line E (maximum $67,800)

cpp2MaxEarnings.label: Most earnings subject to second additional contributions
cpp2MaxEarnings.source: Schedule 8, Part 2, line C: $9,900 for 12 months

cppEarningsPerContribution.label: Earnings that a dollar of employee base and first additional contributions covers

cpp2EmployeeRate.label: Second additional CPP rate for employees

cppSelfEmployedBaseRate.label: Base CPP rate on self-employment earnings

cppSelfEmployedFirstRate.label: First additional CPP rate on self-employment earnings

cppSelfEmployedSecondRate.label: Second additional CPP rate on self-employment earnings

childCareUnder7.label: Child care limit for a child born in 2019 or later

childCare7to16.label: Child care limit for a child born in 2009 to 2018

foreignPropertyTaxRate.label: Most foreign tax on property income that counts for the credit
foreignPropertyTaxRate.source: Income Tax Act 20(11) and Form T2209: foreign tax on property income above 15% is deducted on line 23200 instead

onTaxBrackets.label: Ontario tax brackets
onTaxBrackets.source: ON428 Part A, bases as printed on the form

onFirstBracketTop.label: Top of the first Ontario bracket
onFirstBracketTop.source: ON428 Part A and ON(S2) line 5: $52,886

onCreditRate.label: Ontario credit rate
onCreditRate.source: ON428 line 45: Ontario non-refundable tax credit rate

onAgeAmountThreshold.label: Net income where the Ontario age amount starts to go down

onSpouseBase.label: Ontario spouse and eligible dependant amount, base

onSpouseMax.label: Ontario spouse and eligible dependant amount, most

onMedicalThresholdMax.label: Ontario medical expense threshold, most
onMedicalThresholdMax.source: ON428 line 40: whichever is less, $2,885 or 3% of net income

onDonationLowRate.label: Ontario donation credit rate on the first $200

onDividendEligibleRate.label: Ontario dividend tax credit rate, eligible dividends
onDividendEligibleRate.source: Worksheet ON428, line 61520: 10% of the taxable amount of eligible dividends

onDividendOtherRate.label: Ontario dividend tax credit rate, other dividends
onDividendOtherRate.source: Worksheet ON428, line 61520: 2.9863% of the taxable amount of other than eligible dividends

onSurtaxThreshold1.label: Ontario surtax, first threshold
onSurtaxThreshold1.source: ON428 line 66: 20% of Ontario tax over $5,710

onSurtaxThreshold2.label: Ontario surtax, second threshold
onSurtaxThreshold2.source: ON428 line 67: 36% of Ontario tax over $7,307

onTaxReductionChild.label: Ontario tax reduction per dependent child
onTaxReductionChild.source: ON428 line 75: $544 for each dependent child born in 2007 or later

liftRate.label: LIFT credit, share of employment income

AB428.17.label: Alberta age amount
AB428.17.formula: if(person.age >= 65, max(0, param.abAgeAmountMax - round(max(0, line.T1.23600 - param.abAgeAmountThreshold) * param.abAgeAmountRate, 2)), 0)
AB428.17.source: Worksheet AB428, line 58080: for people born in 1960 or earlier

AB428.20.label: Alberta spouse or common-law partner amount

AB428.23.label: Alberta amount for an eligible dependant
AB428.23.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 0 and household.childrenUnder18 > 0, max(0, param.abSpouseBase - answer.dependantNetIncome), 0)
AB428.23.source: AB428 lines 21 to 23: the base minus their net income

AB428.32.label: CPP and EI credit amounts
AB428.32.source: AB428 lines 27 to 32: lines 30800, 31000 and 31200 of your return

AB428.34.label: Alberta pension income amount
AB428.34.source: AB428 line 34 (58360): eligible pension income, up to $1,719

AB428.42.label: Amounts transferred from your spouse or common-law partner
AB428.42.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear, if(spouse.person.age >= 65 or spouse.line.AB428.34 > 0, unsupported("Transferring your spouse's unused Alberta age or pension amount (Schedule AB(S2)) isn't handled by this app yet"), 0), 0)

AB428.49.label: Allowable medical expenses
AB428.49.source: AB428 lines 44 to 49: expenses over whichever is less, $2,884 or 3% of net income

AB428.52.label: Alberta credit amounts
AB428.52.formula: line.AB428.16 + line.AB428.17 + line.AB428.20 + line.AB428.23 + line.AB428.32 + line.AB428.34 + line.AB428.42 + line.AB428.49

AB428.54.label: Alberta credit amounts at the credit rate

AB428.57.label: Alberta donations credit
AB428.57.source: AB428 lines 55 to 57: Schedule 9 lines 13 and 14 at 60% and 21%

AB428.74.label: Alberta supplemental tax credit
AB428.74.source: Worksheet AB428, line 61545: credit amounts (less unused tuition) at 8%, over $4,800, at 25%

AB.taxOtherwise.label: Alberta tax otherwise payable, for the foreign tax credit
AB.taxOtherwise.source: Form T2036, note 4: AB428 line 63 plus line 68

AB428.69.label: Provincial foreign tax credit
AB428.69.formula: if(line.FTC.left > 0 and line.T1.23600 > 0, min(line.FTC.left, round(min(line.FTC.netForeign, line.T1.23600) * line.AB.taxOtherwise / line.T1.23600, 2), line.AB.taxOtherwise), 0)

AB428.70.label: Alberta tax after the foreign tax credit

BC428.8.label: British Columbia tax on taxable income

BC428.17.label: British Columbia age amount
BC428.17.formula: if(person.age >= 65, max(0, param.bcAgeAmountMax - round(max(0, line.T1.23600 - param.bcAgeAmountThreshold) * param.bcAgeAmountRate, 2)), 0)
BC428.17.source: Worksheet BC428, line 58080: for people born in 1960 or earlier

BC428.20.label: British Columbia spouse or common-law partner amount

BC428.23.label: British Columbia amount for an eligible dependant
BC428.23.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 0 and household.childrenUnder18 > 0, min(param.bcSpouseMax, max(0, param.bcSpouseBase - answer.dependantNetIncome)), 0)
BC428.23.source: BC428 lines 21 to 23: the base minus their net income, up to the maximum

BC428.33.label: CPP and EI credit amounts
BC428.33.source: BC428 lines 27 to 33: lines 30800, 31000 and 31200 of your return

BC428.36.label: British Columbia pension income amount
BC428.36.source: BC428 line 36 (58360): eligible pension income, up to $1,000

BC428.44.label: Amounts transferred from your spouse or common-law partner
BC428.44.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear, if(spouse.person.age >= 65 or spouse.line.BC428.36 > 0, unsupported("Transferring your spouse's unused British Columbia age or pension amount (Schedule BC(S2)) isn't handled by this app yet"), 0), 0)

BC428.51.label: Allowable medical expenses
BC428.51.source: BC428 lines 46 to 51: expenses over whichever is less, $2,689 or 3% of net income

BC428.54.label: British Columbia credit amounts
BC428.54.formula: line.BC428.16 + line.BC428.17 + line.BC428.20 + line.BC428.23 + line.BC428.33 + line.BC428.36 + line.BC428.44 + line.BC428.51

BC428.56.label: British Columbia credit amounts at the credit rate

BC428.57.label: British Columbia donations credit
BC428.57.formula: round(min(line.S9.14, max(0, line.T1.26000 - param.bcDonationTopThreshold)) * param.bcDonationTopRate, 2) + round((line.S9.14 - min(line.S9.14, max(0, line.T1.26000 - param.bcDonationTopThreshold))) * param.bcDonationHighRate, 2) + round(line.S9.13 * param.bcDonationLowRate, 2)
BC428.57.source: Worksheet BC428, line 58969: the first $200 at 5.06%, the rest at 16.8%, or 20.5% up to taxable income over $259,829

BC428.79.label: British Columbia tax reduction
BC428.79.formula: if(line.T1.23600 >= param.bcTaxReductionLimit, 0, max(0, param.bcTaxReductionBasic - round(max(0, line.T1.23600 - param.bcTaxReductionBase) * param.bcTaxReductionRate, 2)))
BC428.79.source: BC428 lines 73 to 79: $562, less 3.56% of net income over $25,020

BC.taxOtherwise.label: British Columbia tax otherwise payable, for the foreign tax credit
BC.taxOtherwise.source: Form T2036, note 4: British Columbia tax without the foreign tax credit

BC428.71.label: Provincial foreign tax credit
BC428.71.formula: if(line.FTC.left > 0 and line.T1.23600 > 0, min(line.FTC.left, round(min(line.FTC.netForeign, line.T1.23600) * line.BC.taxOtherwise / line.T1.23600, 2), line.BC.taxOtherwise), 0)

BC428.72.label: British Columbia tax after the foreign tax credit

HH.partner.label: Spouse or common-law partner on December 31 (1 for yes)

SPOUSES.together.label: Both spouses' returns are prepared here (1 for yes)

HH.spouseNetIncome.label: Your spouse's or partner's net income
HH.spouseNetIncome.source: From their return when both returns are prepared here; otherwise from your answer

T1.10400.label: Other employment income
T1.10400.source: Employment income earned outside Canada, in Canadian dollars

T1.11500.label: Other pensions and superannuation
T1.11500.source: T4A box 016; annuities (T4A box 024) and RRIF payments (T4RIF box 16) at 65 or older, else on line 13000

T1.12000.label: Taxable amount of dividends (eligible and other than eligible)
T1.12000.source: Federal Worksheet, line 12000: boxes 11 and 25 of T5 slips, boxes 32 and 50 of T3 slips

T1.12010.label: Taxable amount of dividends other than eligible

T1.12100.label: Interest and other investment income
T1.12100.source: Federal Worksheet, line 12100: box 13 of T5 slips, box 25 of T3 slips, and foreign interest and dividends

T1.12600.label: Net rental income
T1.12600.source: Form T776, line 9369: rents less expenses. Capital cost allowance isn't claimed

T1.12700.label: Taxable capital gains
T1.12700.source: Schedule 3. A net capital loss isn't entered here; it carries forward

T1.13000.label: Other income
T1.13000.source: Box 26 of T3 slips; annuities and RRIF payments before 65

SE.net.label: Net self-employment income
SE.net.source: Form T2125, line 9369: gross income less expenses. Capital cost allowance isn't claimed

SCOPE.income.label: Income this app doesn't handle
SCOPE.income.formula: if(answer.soldProperty, if(answer.propertyUse == "principal_residence_some_years", unsupported("A home that was your principal residence for only some of the years you owned it (Form T2091) isn't handled by this app yet"), if(answer.propertyUse == "flipped", unsupported("A home owned less than 12 months (a flipped property) is business income, which this app doesn't handle yet"), 0)), 0)

T1.21200.label: Annual union, professional, or like dues

CC.expenses.label: Child care expenses paid
CC.expenses.source: Form T778, line 67950: receipts, and the amount entered that isn't on one

CC.limit.label: Basic limit for child care expenses
CC.limit.source: Form T778, Part B, lines 1 to 4. Children with a disability ($11,000) aren't handled

CC.earned.label: Earned income
CC.earned.source: Form T778, line 6: employment income and net self-employment income

CC.netIncome.label: Net income without the child care deduction

CC.spouseNetIncome.label: Your spouse's or partner's net income without it

T1.21400.label: Child care expenses
T1.21400.formula: if(answer.hasChildCare, if(line.HH.partner == 1 and line.CC.netIncome > line.CC.spouseNetIncome, unsupported("Only the spouse or partner with the lower net income claims child care expenses, except in the cases of Form T778, Part C. Enter them on the other return"), min(line.CC.expenses, line.CC.limit, round(line.CC.earned * 2 / 3, 2))), 0)
T1.21400.source: Form T778, Part B, line 7: whichever is least, the basic limit, the expenses, or 2/3 of earned income

T1.21900.label: Moving expenses
T1.21900.source: Form T1-M, line 29: net moving expenses up to the net eligible income at the new location

T1.22200.label: Deduction for CPP contributions on self-employment income
T1.22200.formula: if(line.CPP.employed > 0, round(line.CPP.base * 0.5, 2) + 2 * round(line.CPP.first * 0.5, 2) + 2 * round(line.CPP.second * 0.5, 2), round(line.CPP.base * 0.5, 2) + line.CPP.first + line.CPP.second)
T1.22200.source: Schedule 8, Part 4 line 17 or Part 5 line 88: half the base contributions, and the additional contributions

T1.22215.label: Deduction for CPP enhanced contributions on employment income
T1.22215.source: Schedule 8 for employees: the first enhancement (1% of 5.95%) and all second CPP contributions are deducted

T1.22900.label: Other employment expenses
T1.22900.formula: if(answer.hasWorkFromHome, min(round(answer.homeOfficeExpenses * answer.homeOfficeShare / 100, 2), max(0, line.T1.10100 + line.T1.10400 - line.T1.20700 - line.T1.21200)), 0)
T1.22900.source: Form T777, lines 48 to 54: home expenses times the employment-use share, up to employment income

DED.foreignTax.label: Foreign tax on foreign interest and dividends above 15% of them
DED.foreignTax.source: Income Tax Act 20(11): deducted on line 23200 instead of counting for the foreign tax credit

T1.23200.label: Other deductions
T1.23200.source: An OAS overpayment recovered (T4A(OAS) box 20), and foreign tax on foreign interest and dividends above 15% of them (Income Tax Act 20(11))

T1.23500.label: Social benefits repayment
T1.23500.formula: if(line.T1.11900 > 0 and sum(T4E.box15) > 0 and line.T1.23400 > param.eiRepaymentThreshold, unsupported("Repaying EI benefits (the chart on your T4E) isn't handled by this app yet"), min(max(0, line.T1.11300 - sum(T4AOAS.box20)), round(max(0, line.T1.23400 - param.oasRecoveryThreshold) * param.oasRecoveryRate, 2)))
T1.23500.source: Federal Worksheet, line 23500: 15% of net income over $93,454, up to the OAS received

CPP.seEarnings.label: Pensionable net self-employment earnings
CPP.seEarnings.formula: if(line.SE.net > 0, if(person.age <= 17 or person.age > 70, 0, if(person.age == 18 or person.age == 70, unsupported("CPP contributions for part of the year (the year you turned 18 or 70) aren't handled by this app yet"), line.SE.net)), 0)

CPP.employed.label: CPP pensionable earnings from employment
CPP.employed.source: Schedule 8, Part 3, line 1: box 26 of T4 slips (box 14 if blank)

CPP.covered.label: Earnings already covered by employment contributions

CPP.exemptionLeft.label: Basic exemption not used by employment

CPP.baseEarnings.label: Self-employment earnings subject to base and first additional contributions
CPP.baseEarnings.formula: max(0, min(line.CPP.seEarnings, max(0, param.cppMaxContributoryEarnings - line.CPP.covered)) - max(0, line.CPP.exemptionLeft - max(0, line.CPP.seEarnings - param.cppMaxContributoryEarnings)))

CPP.secondEarnings.label: Self-employment earnings subject to second additional contributions
CPP.secondEarnings.formula: if(line.CPP.seEarnings + min(param.cppAdditionalMaxPensionableEarnings, line.CPP.employed) > param.cppMaxPensionableEarnings, max(0, min(param.cpp2MaxEarnings - round(sum(T4.box16A) / param.cpp2EmployeeRate, 2), line.CPP.seEarnings - line.CPP.exemptionLeft - line.CPP.baseEarnings)), 0)

CPP.base.label: Base CPP contributions on self-employment earnings

CPP.first.label: First additional CPP contributions on self-employment earnings

CPP.second.label: Second additional CPP contributions on self-employment earnings

T1.30000.label: Basic personal amount
T1.30000.formula:
round(param.basicPersonalAmountMax
  - (param.basicPersonalAmountMax - param.basicPersonalAmountMin)
  * clamp(line.T1.23600 - param.basicPersonalAmountPhaseStart, 0, param.basicPersonalAmountPhaseEnd - param.basicPersonalAmountPhaseStart)
  / (param.basicPersonalAmountPhaseEnd - param.basicPersonalAmountPhaseStart), 2)
T1.30000.source: Federal Worksheet, line 30000: the full amount up to the 26% bracket, going down to the minimum at the 33% bracket

T1.30100.label: Age amount
T1.30100.formula: if(person.age >= 65, max(0, param.ageAmountMax - round(max(0, line.T1.23600 - param.ageAmountThreshold) * param.ageAmountRate, 2)), 0)
T1.30100.source: Federal Worksheet, line 30100: for people born in 1960 or earlier

T1.30300.label: Spouse or common-law partner amount
T1.30300.source: Schedule 5 line 30300: your basic personal amount minus their net income

T1.30400.label: Amount for an eligible dependant
T1.30400.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 0 and household.childrenUnder18 > 0, max(0, line.T1.30000 - answer.dependantNetIncome), 0)
T1.30400.source: Schedule 5 line 30400: for a single parent, one child under 18 who lived with you: your basic personal amount minus their net income

T1.30800.label: Base CPP contributions through employment
T1.30800.source: Schedule 8 for employees: the base part (4.95% of 5.95%) is a credit

T1.31000.label: CPP contributions on self-employment income
T1.31000.source: Schedule 8, Part 5, line 70: half the base contributions

T1.31400.label: Pension income amount
T1.31400.source: Federal Worksheet, line 31400: eligible pension income on line 11500, up to $2,000

T1.32600.label: Amounts transferred from your spouse or common-law partner
T1.32600.source: Schedule 2: their unused age amount and the tuition they designate to you

T1.33099.label: Medical expenses for you, your spouse and your children
T1.33099.formula: if(household.partnerInYear and spouse.answer.claimSpouseMedical and line.HH.partner == 1, 0, line.OWN.medical) + if(household.partnerInYear and answer.claimSpouseMedical and line.HH.partner == 1, spouse.line.OWN.medical, 0)
T1.33099.source: Either spouse can claim the family's medical expenses: this return's own, unless the spouse claims them, and the spouse's when this return claims them

OWN.medical.label: Medical expenses on this return's receipts and entered here
OWN.medical.source: Medical expense receipts, and the amount entered that isn't on one

T1.33200.label: Allowable medical expenses
T1.33200.source: T1 lines 107 to 112: expenses over whichever is less, $2,834 or 3% of net income

T1.33800.label: Credit amounts at the credit rate

T1.34990.label: Top-up tax credit
T1.34990.source: Federal Worksheet, line 34990: keeps credit amounts above the first bracket at 15%

T1.40425.label: Federal dividend tax credit
T1.40425.source: Federal Worksheet, line 40425: the credit as shown on the slips

FTC.netForeign.label: Net foreign non-business income
FTC.netForeign.source: Form T2209, note 2: the foreign income less the foreign tax deducted under 20(11) (part of line 23200)

FTC.eligibleTax.label: Non-business income tax paid to a foreign country
FTC.eligibleTax.source: Form T2209, line 1: foreign tax on interest and dividends counts up to 15% of them

FTC.basicFederalTax.label: Basic federal tax, for the foreign tax credit
FTC.basicFederalTax.source: Form T2209, note 4: line 42900 plus the federal dividend tax credit

T1.40500.label: Federal foreign tax credit
T1.40500.formula: if(line.FTC.eligibleTax > 0 and line.T1.23600 > 0, min(line.FTC.eligibleTax, round(min(line.FTC.netForeign, line.T1.23600) * line.FTC.basicFederalTax / line.T1.23600, 2), line.T1.42900), 0)
T1.40500.source: Form T2209, line 3: the foreign tax, up to the share of basic federal tax on the foreign income

FTC.left.label: Foreign tax left for the provincial credit

T1.42800.label: Provincial tax
T1.42800.formula: if(person.province == "ON", line.ON428.90, if(person.province == "BC", line.BC428.91, if(person.province == "AB", line.AB428.75, unsupported("Provincial tax for this province isn't handled by this app"))))

T1.42100.label: CPP contributions payable on self-employment income

T1.43700.label: Total income tax deducted
T1.43700.formula: sum(T4.box22) + sum(T4A.box022) + sum(T4AP.box22) + sum(T4AOAS.box22) + sum(T4E.box22) + sum(T4RIF.box28)
T1.43700.source: The income tax deducted on all slips

T1.44800.label: CPP overpayment
T1.44800.formula: if(sum(T4.box16) > param.cppEmployeeMax or sum(T4.box16A) > param.cpp2EmployeeMax, unsupported("More CPP was deducted than the 2025 maximum. The overpayment (Schedule 8) isn't handled by this app yet"), 0)

T1.45000.label: Employment insurance overpayment
T1.45000.formula: if(sum(T4.box18) > param.eiPremiumMax, unsupported("More EI was deducted than the 2025 maximum. The overpayment isn't handled by this app yet"), 0)

S2.6.label: Their age amount, pension income amount, and the tuition they designate to you

S2.7.label: Their taxable income, for the transfer

S2.11.label: Their basic personal amount, CPP, EI and employment amounts, and tuition
S2.11.formula: spouse.line.T1.30000 + spouse.line.T1.30800 + spouse.line.T1.31000 + spouse.line.T1.31200 + spouse.line.T1.31260 + spouse.line.T1.32300
S2.11.source: Schedule 2 lines 8 to 11: their lines 30000, 96 and 32300

S2.13.label: Federal amounts transferred from your spouse or common-law partner

S3.13200.label: Gain or loss on publicly traded shares and mutual fund units
S3.13200.formula: if(count(T5008.box20) != count(T5008.box21), unsupported("A T5008 without its cost or book value (box 20) or its proceeds (box 21) can't be counted. Brokers often leave the cost blank: type it from your records into the slip's box 20 on the Confirm step"), sum(T5008.box21) - sum(T5008.box20))
S3.13200.source: Schedule 3 line 4: proceeds (T5008 box 21) minus cost or book value (box 20)

S3.13800.label: Gain or loss on real estate
S3.13800.source: Schedule 3 line 5: proceeds less the adjusted cost base and selling costs. A home that was your principal residence every year has no gain (Form T2091)

S3.15800.label: Gain on personal-use property
S3.15800.formula: if(answer.soldProperty, if(answer.propertyUse == "personal_use", max(0, answer.propertyProceeds - answer.propertyCost - answer.propertyOutlays), 0), 0)
S3.15800.source: Schedule 3 line 8: a cottage or other property for your own use. A loss on it isn't allowed

S3.19900.label: Taxable capital gains or net capital loss

S9.5.label: Total eligible amount of charitable donations
S9.5.formula: if(household.partnerInYear and spouse.answer.claimSpouseDonations and line.HH.partner == 1, 0, line.OWN.donations) + if(household.partnerInYear and answer.claimSpouseDonations and line.HH.partner == 1, spouse.line.OWN.donations, 0)
S9.5.source: Schedule 9 line 5: either spouse can claim both spouses' donations

OWN.donations.label: Donations on this return's receipts and entered here
OWN.donations.source: Official receipts (uploaded, or entered), and box 46 of T4 slips

S9.10.label: Donations claimed (within the limit)
S9.10.source: Schedule 9 lines 6 to 10: up to 75% of net income

S9.19.label: Taxable income in the top bracket

S11.8.label: Tuition fees for 2025
S11.8.source: Schedule 11 lines 1 to 8: eligible fees from T2202 box 26. The Canada training credit isn't claimed

S11.9.label: Unused federal tuition from your 2024 notice of assessment

S11.11.label: Income the tuition amount can reduce to zero tax
S11.11.source: Schedule 11 line 11: taxable income, or above $57,375, federal tax on taxable income ÷ 14.5%

S11.23.label: Tuition you can transfer
S11.23.source: Schedule 11 lines 21 to 23: this year's tuition up to $5,000, less what you used

S11.24.label: Tuition transferred to your spouse or common-law partner
S11.24.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear and line.S11.8 > 0, min(answer.tuitionTransfer, line.S11.23), 0)
S11.24.source: Schedule 11 line 24: the amount you designate on your T2202, up to line 23

SUGGEST.rrspDeduction.label: RRSP contributions you can deduct for 2025
SUGGEST.rrspDeduction.formula: if(sum(NOA.box1) > 0, min(sum(RRSP.box1) + sum(RRSP.box2) + sum(NOA.box2), sum(NOA.box1)), sum(RRSP.box1) + sum(RRSP.box2) + sum(NOA.box2))
SUGGEST.rrspDeduction.source: RRSP receipts, and the unused contributions and deduction limit on your 2024 notice of assessment

ON428.10.label: Ontario age amount
ON428.10.formula: if(person.age >= 65, max(0, param.onAgeAmountMax - round(max(0, line.T1.23600 - param.onAgeAmountThreshold) * param.onAgeAmountRate, 2)), 0)
ON428.10.source: Worksheet ON428, line 58080: for people born in 1960 or earlier

ON428.13.label: Ontario spouse or common-law partner amount

ON428.16.label: Ontario amount for an eligible dependant
ON428.16.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 0 and household.childrenUnder18 > 0, min(param.onSpouseMax, max(0, param.onSpouseBase - answer.dependantNetIncome)), 0)
ON428.16.source: ON428 lines 14 to 16: the base minus their net income, up to the maximum

ON428.24.label: CPP and EI credit amounts
ON428.24.source: ON428 lines 19 to 24: lines 30800, 31000 and 31200 of your return

ON428.27.label: Ontario pension income amount
ON428.27.source: ON428 line 27 (58360): eligible pension income, up to $1,762

ON428.41.label: Allowable medical expenses
ON428.41.source: ON428 lines 36 to 41: expenses over whichever is less, $2,885 or 3% of net income

ON428.34.label: Ontario amounts transferred from your spouse or common-law partner
ON428.34.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 1 and household.partnerInYear, if(spouse.line.ON428.10 + spouse.line.ON428.27 == 0, 0, if(spouse.person.province == "ON", line.ONS2.11, unsupported("Your spouse lives in another province: transferring their Ontario age or pension amount isn't handled by this app"))), 0)
ON428.34.source: Schedule ON(S2): their unused Ontario age and pension income amounts

ON428.44.label: Ontario credit amounts
ON428.44.formula: line.ON428.9 + line.ON428.10 + line.ON428.13 + line.ON428.16 + line.ON428.24 + line.ON428.27 + line.ON428.34 + line.ON428.41

ON428.46.label: Ontario credit amounts at the credit rate

ON428.49.label: Ontario donations credit
ON428.49.source: ON428 lines 47 to 49: Schedule 9 lines 13 and 14 at 5.05% and 11.16%

ON428.68.label: Ontario surtax
ON428.68.formula: round(max(0, line.ON428.53 - param.onSurtaxThreshold1) * param.onSurtaxRate1, 2) + round(max(0, line.ON428.53 - param.onSurtaxThreshold2) * param.onSurtaxRate2, 2)
ON428.68.source: ON428 lines 63 to 68, on Ontario tax after credits (line 62)

ON428.73.label: Ontario tax after surtax and the dividend credit

ON428.75.label: Ontario tax reduction for dependent children
ON428.75.formula: if(line.HH.partner == 1 and line.HH.spouseNetIncome > line.T1.23600, 0, param.onTaxReductionChild * household.childrenUnder19)
ON428.75.source: ON428 line 75: $544 per child born in 2007 or later, claimed by the spouse with the higher net income

ON428.80.label: Ontario tax reduction
ON428.80.source: ON428 lines 74 to 80: twice the reductions, less Ontario tax

ON428.85.label: Low-income individuals and families tax (LIFT) credit
ON428.85.source: ON428-A Part A when single, Part B with a spouse or partner

ON.taxOtherwise.label: Ontario tax otherwise payable, for the foreign tax credit
ON.taxOtherwise.formula: max(0, line.ON428.53 + line.ON428.68 - if(line.ON428.53 + line.ON428.68 == 0, 0, max(0, 2 * (param.onTaxReductionBasic + line.ON428.75) - (line.ON428.53 + line.ON428.68))))
ON.taxOtherwise.source: Form T2036, note 4: ON428 line 81 worked out with lines 70 and 72 at zero

ON428.82.label: Provincial foreign tax credit
ON428.82.formula: if(line.FTC.left > 0 and line.T1.23600 > 0, min(line.FTC.left, round(min(line.FTC.netForeign, line.T1.23600) * line.ON.taxOtherwise / line.T1.23600, 2), line.ON.taxOtherwise), 0)

ON428.83.label: Ontario tax after the foreign tax credit

ON428.86.label: Ontario tax after the LIFT credit

ON428.89.label: Ontario health premium
ON428.89.source: ON428 line 89 chart: $0 to $900 by taxable income, in steps at $20,000, $36,000, $48,000, $72,000 and $200,000

ON428A.5.label: LIFT credit before the income test
ON428A.5.source: ON428-A lines 1 to 5: lines 10100 and 10400 at 5.05%, up to $875

ON428A.13.label: Adjusted net income
ON428A.13.source: ON428-A lines 6 to 13: net income (line 23600) before it was floored at zero

ON428A.28.label: Your spouse's or partner's adjusted net income
ON428A.28.source: ON428-A line 28: from their return, or your answer for their net income

ON428A.38.label: Income over the LIFT thresholds
ON428A.38.formula: max(max(0, line.ON428A.13 - param.liftThreshold), max(0, line.ON428A.13 + line.ON428A.28 - param.liftFamilyThreshold))
ON428A.38.source: ON428-A Part B lines 30 to 38: the greater of your income over $32,500 and family income over $65,000

ON428A.41.label: LIFT credit, with a spouse or partner

ONS2.5.label: Their taxable income, for the transfer

ONS2.11.label: Ontario amounts transferred from your spouse

hasEmploymentIncome.help: A T4 from each employer you worked for in 2025.

hasInvestmentIncome.help: A T5 from each bank, credit union or broker that paid you $50 or more.

hasTrustIncome.help: A T3 from each mutual fund or trust held outside an RRSP or TFSA.

hasSoldInvestments.ask: Sold shares, bonds or fund units
hasSoldInvestments.help: A T5008 from each broker, for sales outside an RRSP or TFSA.

hasCppBenefits.help: A T4A(P) from Service Canada, for a CPP retirement, survivor or disability pension.

hasPensionIncome.ask: A workplace pension or an annuity
hasPensionIncome.help: A T4A from each pension plan or payer.

hasRrifIncome.help: A T4RIF from each registered retirement income fund you were paid from.

hasEiBenefits.help: A T4E from Service Canada, for EI regular, sickness, maternity or parental benefits.

hasSelfEmployment.help: Income from your own business, freelancing or gig work (Form T2125). Attach a T2125 to a paper return.

optionLabels.business: Business (a shop, trade or gig work)

selfEmploymentGross.help: What you were paid in 2025, without GST/HST you collected.

selfEmploymentExpenses.help: Supplies, rent, phone, travel, fees and other costs of earning it. Capital cost allowance isn't claimed.

hasRentalIncome.help: Rent from a property you own (Form T776). If you own it with someone, enter your share.

rentalExpenses.help: Mortgage interest, property tax, insurance, repairs, utilities you paid, and fees. Capital cost allowance isn't claimed.

hasForeignIncome.help: Interest, dividends or employment income earned abroad, in Canadian dollars. Foreign tax paid on it gives a foreign tax credit (Form T2209).

hasForeignProperty.ask: Property outside Canada that cost more than $100,000
hasForeignProperty.help: Foreign bank accounts, shares or real estate (not a home you use) that cost more than $100,000 in total at any time in 2025.
hasForeignProperty.note: File Form T1135, Foreign Income Verification Statement, with your return. It reports the property; it doesn't change your tax. This app doesn't prepare it.

soldProperty.ask: Sold your home or other real estate
soldProperty.help: The sale of a home, cottage or rental property in 2025 (Schedule 3; Form T2091 for a home).

optionLabels.principal_residence: Your home, every year you owned it
optionLabels.principal_residence_some_years: Your home, but only some of the years
optionLabels.personal_use: A cottage or other property for your own use

propertyCost.ask: What you paid for it, with improvements
propertyCost.help: The adjusted cost base: the purchase price, the costs of buying, and the cost of improvements.

propertyOutlays.help: Real estate commission, legal fees and other costs of selling.

rrspDeduction.help: Contributions from March 4, 2025 to March 2, 2026, up to your limit on last year's notice of assessment.

hasWorkFromHome.help: Home-office expenses as an employee who worked from home more than half the time for at least 4 weeks in a row (Form T777). Your employer must sign Form T2200; keep it.

homeOfficeExpenses.help: Electricity, heat, water, home internet, maintenance and rent for your whole home. Mortgage interest and property tax don't count.

homeOfficeShare.help: The workspace's share of your home's area, times its share of the week's hours used for work. 12% of the area for 40 of 168 hours is 2.86%.

hasChildCare.help: Daycare, before- and after-school programs or day camps, so you could work (Form T778). For a couple, the one with the lower net income claims it.

childCareExpenses.help: Uploaded receipts are added; enter what isn't on one.

hasMovingExpenses.help: A move at least 40 km closer to a new job or business (Form T1-M).

movingExpenses.help: Movers, travel, up to 15 days of temporary living, and the costs of selling your old home and buying the new one, less what your employer paid back.

movingIncome.ask: Income earned at the new location
movingIncome.help: Employment or self-employment income from the new job or business in 2025, less its deductions (union dues, CPP).

hasTuition.ask: Tuition at a college or university
hasTuition.help: A T2202 from each school, for 2025.

unusedTuition.ask: Unused federal tuition from your 2024 notice of assessment

tuitionTransfer.ask: Tuition to transfer to your spouse or partner
tuitionTransfer.help: Up to $5,000 of this year's tuition, as designated on the back of your T2202.

medicalExpenses.help: For you, your spouse or your children. Uploaded receipts are added; enter what isn't on one. Either spouse can claim the family's medical expenses; it usually saves more on the lower income.

donations.help: On official receipts. Uploaded receipts and box 46 of your T4 are added; enter what isn't on one. Either spouse can claim both spouses' donations; claiming them together usually saves more.

dependantNetIncome.help: The net income (line 23600 of their return, if they file one) of the child you claim the amount for an eligible dependant for. The amount goes down by it. Don't add it if they had no income.

spouseNetIncome.ask: Your spouse's or partner's 2025 net income
spouseNetIncome.help: Line 23600 of their return. Their return isn't prepared here, but some of your credits depend on it.

claimSpouseDonations.ask: Claim your spouse's or partner's donations on this return

claimSpouseMedical.ask: Claim your spouse's or partner's medical expenses on this return

T4.title: T4 Statement of Remuneration Paid
T4.about: Employment income an employer paid, and the tax, CPP, EI and dues it withheld

T5.title: T5 Statement of Investment Income
T5.about: Interest, dividends and capital gains dividends from a bank, broker or corporation

boxes.10: Actual amount of dividends other than eligible dividends
boxes.11: Taxable amount of dividends other than eligible dividends
boxes.12: Dividend tax credit for dividends other than eligible dividends
boxes.26: Dividend tax credit for eligible dividends

T3.title: T3 Statement of Trust Income Allocations and Designations
T3.about: Income a trust or mutual fund allocated to you, such as capital gains, dividends and other income

boxes.23: Actual amount of dividends other than eligible dividends
boxes.32: Taxable amount of dividends other than eligible dividends
boxes.39: Dividend tax credit for dividends other than eligible dividends
boxes.51: Dividend tax credit for eligible dividends

T5008.title: T5008 Statement of Securities Transactions
T5008.about: A sale of shares, bonds or fund units through a broker, with the proceeds and, when the broker knows it, the cost

boxes.21: Proceeds of disposition or settlement amount

T2202.title: T2202 Tuition and Enrolment Certificate
T2202.about: Eligible tuition fees a college or university received, and the months of study

T4AOAS.title: T4A(OAS) Statement of Old Age Security
T4AOAS.about: Old Age Security pension paid in the year by Service Canada, and the tax deducted from it
T4AOAS.name: T4A(OAS)

T4AP.title: T4A(P) Statement of Canada Pension Plan Benefits
T4AP.about: Canada Pension Plan benefits paid in the year (retirement, survivor, disability), and the tax deducted from them
T4AP.name: T4A(P)

T4A.title: T4A Statement of Pension, Retirement, Annuity, and Other Income
T4A.about: A workplace pension, an annuity or other income from a pension plan or payer, and the tax deducted from it

boxes.105: Scholarships, bursaries, fellowships, artists' project grants and prizes

T4RIF.title: T4RIF Statement of Income from a Registered Retirement Income Fund
T4RIF.about: Payments from a registered retirement income fund (RRIF), and the tax deducted from them

T4E.title: T4E Statement of Employment Insurance and Other Benefits
T4E.about: Employment insurance benefits paid in the year, and the tax deducted from them

RRSP.title: RRSP contribution receipt
RRSP.about: Contributions to a registered retirement savings plan, from the plan's issuer, for March 4, 2025 to March 2, 2026 (contributions from January 1 to March 3, 2025 belong to the 2024 return)

DONATION.title: Official donation receipt
DONATION.about: A receipt for income tax purposes from a registered charity or other qualified donee, for a gift made in 2025

CHILDCARE.title: Child care receipt
CHILDCARE.about: A receipt from a daycare, day camp, school program or caregiver for looking after a child in 2025

MEDICAL.title: Medical expense receipt
MEDICAL.about: A receipt for medical or dental care, prescriptions or devices paid for in 2025, for you, your spouse or your children

NOA.title: Notice of assessment for 2024
NOA.about: The CRA's notice of assessment for last year's (2024) return, which carries the RRSP deduction limit and the amounts to carry forward to 2025

boxes.2: Unused RRSP contributions available to deduct for 2025
boxes.3: Unused federal tuition, education and textbook amounts available for 2025

poolDonations.title: Claim both spouses' donations on one return
poolDonations.text: The first $200 of donations each year gets a lower credit. Claiming both spouses' donations on one return uses that lower rate once instead of twice. Your spouse's or partner's donations are then claimed on this return and left off theirs.
poolDonations.when: line.SPOUSES.together == 1 and spouse.line.OWN.donations > 0 and not answer.claimSpouseDonations

medicalOnOneReturn.title: Claim the family's medical expenses on this return
medicalOnOneReturn.text: Medical expenses count only above 3% of the claimant's net income (or $2,834, if less), so they usually save more on the return with the lower income. Your spouse's or partner's medical expenses are then claimed on this return and left off theirs.
medicalOnOneReturn.when: line.SPOUSES.together == 1 and spouse.line.OWN.medical > 0 and not answer.claimSpouseMedical
medicalOnOneReturn.amountLabel: Your spouse's or partner's medical expenses

tuitionTransfer.title: Transfer tuition you don't need to your spouse or partner
tuitionTransfer.text: You can transfer up to $5,000 of this year's tuition that this return doesn't use to your spouse or partner. Sign the transfer on the back of your T2202. The amount is saved as "Tuition to transfer to your spouse or partner" on Credits.

rrspNowOrLater.title: You can deduct your RRSP contributions in a later year
rrspNowOrLater.text: Your taxable income is in the lowest federal bracket. You don't have to deduct all your RRSP contributions for 2025: what you don't deduct carries forward, and may save more in a year when your income is higher. To deduct less, change the amount on Deductions.

rrspOverContribution.title: Your RRSP contributions may be over your limit
rrspOverContribution.text: Your contributions are more than your RRSP deduction limit on your 2024 notice of assessment plus $2,000. The CRA charges a tax of 1% a month on the excess until it is withdrawn, on form T1-OVP. This app doesn't prepare that form. Check your limit, and the contributions you made after your notice of assessment.
rrspOverContribution.when: sum(NOA.box1) > 0 and sum(RRSP.box1) + sum(RRSP.box2) + sum(NOA.box2) > sum(NOA.box1) + param.rrspOverContributionAllowance

interestWithoutSlip.title: Interest is taxable even without a T5
interestWithoutSlip.text: A bank or credit union issues a T5 only when it pays you $50 or more. Interest under that is still income. If you earned any, enter it as a T5 on Income, from your account statements.
